notes: Not a released variety. dhan67 already carried one salt-tolerance mechanism; KASP stacking made it 'highly salt tolerant' (DU/BRRI, 2021).

Pedigree Peta x Dee-geo-woo-gen (line IR8-288-3); named 28 Nov 1966. The 'miracle rice' that launched the Green Revolution; IRRI's first variety; carries sd1. Susceptible to blast, BLB, tungro, grassy stunt. IRRI booklet notes qualitative salinity tolerance (no dS/m given).

Pedigree IR1561-228-1-2/IR1737//CR94-13 (ancestry incl. IR8, IR24, O. nivara). Multiple disease/insect resistance incl. BPH biotype 2 (bph-2); planted on >10 m ha in the 1980s. Named an All-India variety in 1981.

Pedigree TN1/T141; first AICRIP-bred variety, notified in 19 states. India's first homegrown high-yielding semi-dwarf of the Green Revolution. Duration, height and yield not verified from accessible sources.

Pedigree Vasista x Mahsuri; developed at Maruteru as the 'successor to Mahsuri' — short-statured, N-responsive, Mahsuri-like grain quality. Mega-variety of rainfed lowlands in eastern India, Nepal terai and Bangladesh; low glycemic index. Susceptible to sheath blight and BPH.
Pedigree GEB 24/TN 1//Mahsuri. Fine-grain medium-slender mega-variety prized for cooking quality; ~1.5 m ha across six states. Highly susceptible to bacterial blight and blast.

Samba Mahsuri*4/SS1113: three bacterial blight resistance genes (Xa21, xa13, xa5) pyramided by marker-assisted backcrossing (not transgenic), retaining grain quality and low GI. Matures about a week earlier than Samba Mahsuri.

IET 10364; cross Pusa 150 x Karnal Local. World's first semi-dwarf, photoperiod-insensitive, high-yielding basmati; extra-long slender aromatic grains (7.38 mm milled, elongation ~2.0). Dominant Indian export basmati of the 1990s.

IET 18004 (line Pusa 1121-92-8-13-3); 1991 cross Pusa 614-1-2 x Pusa 614-2-4-3 with Basmati 370 and Type 3 as quality donors. World's longest milled grain (9.0 mm); elongation ratio ~2.5-2.7; grown on ~70% of India's basmati area. Notified for Punjab/Haryana in 2008.
IET 21960; cross Pusa 1301 x Pusa Basmati 1121; notified S.O. 2817(E) 19 Sept 2013. First early-maturing basmati (~120 days), saving ~5-6 irrigations (~33% water) with PB1121-level grain quality.

Cross IR8 x IARI-5901-2 (spontaneous dwarf mutant from the Assam collection). Non-aromatic semi-dwarf mega variety of NW India; replaced IR8 and Jaya in Punjab/Haryana. Now non-recommended in Punjab (2023) over long duration, water use and stubble burning.

Parmal (non-basmati) rice; resistant to 7 of 10 prevalent bacterial blight pathotypes; short duration (93-95 days after transplanting) with low water need. Covered ~43% of Punjab's rice area by 2024; PAU's promoted Pusa-44 replacement.

Cross IR 50/Improved White Ponni. Short-duration fine-grain rice of Tamil Nadu with medium slender grains; resistant to green leaf hopper, moderately resistant to stem borer and gall midge. Predominant Kuruvai-season variety.

IET 21605 (culture CB 06 535); hybrid derivative of ADT 43/RR 272-1745 (cross 2003, stabilized F5). Semi-dwarf early-duration fine-grain rice; mean trial yield 6623 kg/ha (~10.7% over ADT 43); moderately resistant to blast, BPH, GLH. Released as ADT 43's replacement.

IET 23832; pedigree IR 73707-45-3-2-3/IR 77080-B-34-3. India's first zinc-biofortified rice: ~22.3-22.6 ppm zinc in polished grain; semi-dwarf, long slender grains; moderately resistant to leaf blast. IIRR dates development to 2015; CVRC release 2016.

IET 24780; ARC 10075 (Assam high-protein donor) x Naveen with three backcrosses to Naveen. India's first high-protein rice (10.3% in milled rice, 15 ppm zinc); 65% head rice recovery. NRRI bulletin says CVRC 2015; achievements page lists 2016.

RAU710-99-22; pedigree Sita/Pusa Basmati-1//Katarni. High-yielding fine-grained quality rice (awnless, 5.03 mm kernels, 66% head rice recovery) for Bihar's irrigated ecosystem; outyielded Pusa Basmati 1 by ~38% in nutrient-use trials.

Old Uttar Pradesh variety (NDUAT Faizabad) with long bold grains; still preferred by farmers for taste, yield and pest/disease resistance. Developer, release year and pedigree not verified from accessible sources.
Released for the plains of Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh. Pedigree and plant height not verified from accessible sources.
Pedigree IR-20 x IR-24; early-maturing (95-105 days) long slender grain variety, resistant to BLB, leaf blast and brown spot, tolerating 7-10 day drought spells. SVRC UP 1982; CVRC 1989.

Old established UP mid-early irrigated variety, used as a check in trials; moderate blast tolerance. Developer, release year and pedigree not verified (a 1971 claim exists only in an unverified lecture deck).

Culture R 320-298, tested as IET 10749. Resistant to gall midge (biotype-1); tolerant to blast, sheath rot, brown spot and bacterial blight; long bold grains favored by the poha industry. For MP, Chhattisgarh, UP and Tripura.
Pedigree Vajram/MTU 7014. High-yielding, tolerant to BPH and blast, with strong seed dormancy. Mega-variety of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

Pedigree Krishnaveni/IR 64; tested as IET 15644. Medium-slender mega-variety with high adaptability; tolerant to BPH and blast. Covered ~85% of Telangana's rabi coarse-rice area in 2021-22. One source cites release as 2000.

World's first superfine-grain aromatic (basmati) F1 hybrid; ~40-45% yield advantage over Pusa Basmati 1 in multi-location trials. For irrigated basmati areas (Delhi, Punjab, Haryana, western UP). Some tables list CVRC notification as 2006.
Three-line hybrid; pedigree IR58025A x KMR-3R. Medium-duration, long-bold grain; 21.3% yield advantage over check Jaya in release trials. Widely used as check/mapping population in QTL research.
Bayer private-sector hybrid, still marketed as Arize 6444 Gold (reformulated Gold version listed at 120-125 days). Medium-slender grain; 73.5% milling recovery.
Pioneer private-sector hybrid; highest-yielding of India's early hybrid era (7.86 t/ha, 28% over check PR 106). Recommended for Haryana, UP, TN, AP, Karnataka; still used as a check in trials.
Bayer private-sector hybrid released by CVRC for eastern and southern India; 22.9% yield advantage over check Jaya in release trials. Preceded PA 6444 by one year.
